title: Washerwomen

title: A Woman's Work
alt: figures placed around a domestic scene in an oil painting
view: The artist grouped people around the domestic space rather than giving each person a separate portrait.
record: The museum records an oil painting made in 1912 and identifies its artist.
limit: The painting shows the artist’s choices. It is not a census of who did this work.

title: Washerwomen at Goyen
alt: painted figures working on a shoreline
view: People and the shore appear together in the painted scene.
record: The catalogue dates the Cleveland-made painting to 1917 and titles the place Goyen.
limit: A painted shore is not a verified plan of its routes or a count of its workers.
itemLine: The signed clip holds maker’s credit and the visible evidence of work under one number.

title: Lace Pillow
alt: a lace pillow with a pinned working pattern
view: The picture shows the pattern sitting on its support rather than loose in a finished garment.

title: Pair of Lace Lappets
alt: two pieces of bobbin lace displayed together
view: This collection view keeps both long pieces in the frame.
record: The museum records early eighteenth-century Brussels bobbin lace and gives the two lappets one accession.
limit: A paired record supplies two pieces. It does not tell us whether both were worked by one person.
itemLine: The signed clip holds the surviving pattern and the recorded materials under one number.

title: Fragment of a Band with Birds and Trees
alt: birds and branching trees worked into a narrow band

material: Bleached linen (est.): needle lace, burato (twined ground and darned in one direction)

title: Sash
alt: repeating blocks of pattern on a long woven sash

record: The museum records this seventeenth- or eighteenth-century sash as a brocade of silk and metal.
limit: The material label does not name the weaver or a particular occasion on which it was worn.

title: Exotic Gold-patterned Silk

material: Silk, gold thread; a combination of two weaves, 2/1 twill and 1/3 twill (lampas)

title: Codex Quetzalecatzin
dateKind: Curatorial making range for the surviving manuscript
alt: a coloured Nahua manuscript with pictorial marks and annotations
view: A single manuscript carries pictorial conventions and later-period Latin-letter glosses. The picture and letters share the sheet.
record: Library of Congress curator John Hessler identifies family land claims and genealogy. Lord-11 Quetzalecatzin is presented as an ancestor, and the glosses name don Alonso and don Matheo. The painter-scribes’ names remain unrecorded.
limit: The depicted claims are evidence of what a family presented. They cannot by themselves settle land rights or establish the name of whoever painted the sheet.
itemLine: The dated manuscript, the claimant family and the names within the glosses have separate places under the same accession.
dimension: The guide shows the whole surviving sheet.
origin: Nahua, from present-day Mexico, with places in the region of Mexico City and Puebla

title: Tamping iron associated with Phineas Gage
dateKind: Museum’s estimated making date of the cast-iron object
alt: an original schematic of a marked iron bar resting on a display support
view: The museum describes an iron bar in a brass and wood mount, with an inscription on the metal. The panel is an original drawing of the mount.
record: The museum credits an unnamed Cavendish blacksmith with making it around 1848. A transcribed inscription names Phineas Gage and is dated 6 January 1850. The catalogue separately records J. M. Harlow’s museum deposit in 1868.
limit: The mounted object and its inscription are different evidence from a clinical history. Neither settles a diagnosis or a complete account of changes in personality.
itemLine: The maker, patient, inscribed date and later museum return remain separate in this guide.
material: Cast iron. Later brass and wood mounting
dimension: The schematic gives the stated features without a reproduction scale.
